payload.headline: Microsoft slips 1.12% to 517.99 on no news; still a hold

summary.thesis: Microsoft is growing faster and earning wider margins, but free cash flow fell from 78.0B to 60.0B, so the price only holds up if earnings, not today's cash flow, set the value.
summary.decision: Hold for the long term and add only near strong support. No swing trade from the middle of the range.

payload.happening: The stock fell 1.12% to 517.99, with no new headlines since the last note. That puts it just under the 50-day average of 519.36 and above the first support zone at 504.96–512.76. The next report is on 2027-01-27, and analysts have raised their next-year EPS estimate to 24.2, up 2.2% in 30 days.
payload.business: The business itself keeps improving. Revenue grew 18.8% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, up from 18.3% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. The weak spot is cash. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on equipment and data centers, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B over the trailing year. That puts the free-cash-flow margin at only 17.31%. The filings note that each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year against 51¢ three years ago, so the heavy spending is not paying back yet. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 29.0B and liquidity is 64.5B. Today's 1.12% drop came with no news, so it moves sentiment only. The new risk headings in the annual report are a disclosure matter, not a change in demand. What is at risk is the payback on the spending. Demand and margins are not at risk today.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply. A cash-flow model built on today's 60.0B of free cash flow gives a base value of 220.42 (bear 182.25, bull 291.45). To justify the current price, that cash flow would need to start growing at 41.7% a year. Even at 30% starting growth, the model gives only 340.19. Against its own history, the stock looks fair: its price-to-sales ratio of 11.1 sits at the 43rd percentile of its last five years. That method gives a range of 475.73 to 535.43, with 592.92 at the high end. On earnings, the stock trades at 27.0 times trailing earnings and 21.4 times next year's estimate. Against peers it is expensive: 11.1 times sales against a peer median of 4.1. The whole gap between the methods comes from one question: does the current spending turn back into cash? I use the own-history range as fair value because the earnings and margin trends support it. The 220.42 cash-flow value is the price if that bet fails.
worth.key_assumption: The spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so earnings (next-year EPS estimate 24.2) are the right basis for value, not today's cash flow.

bull: Growth is speeding up, not slowing: quarterly revenue growth reached 18.8%, up from 18.3% two quarters ago.
Margins are widening: operating margin rose to 47.1% from 46.27%.
Analysts keep raising forecasts: the next-year EPS estimate rose to 24.2, up 2.7% in 90 days, which brings the forward P/E down to 21.4.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and the cash-flow base value is only 220.42.
The price needs 41.7% starting growth in free cash flow; at 20% the model gives 234.34.
It trades at 11.1 times sales against a peer median of 4.1, which leaves little room for a miss.

levels.what: Today's close sits inside the 475.73–535.43 fair range. That gives no reason to sell and no margin of safety for new money.
Top of the strongest support zone (486.0–491.22, 8 touches), near the 475.73 own-history low. Adding makes sense here.
Top of the upper resistance zone, on the way toward the 592.92 own-history high. Above it, the case for trimming grows.

longterm.why: The business is improving, but two of three valuation measures lean expensive because cash flow is weak. Today's drop with no news does not change that balance.

swing.why: The price sits inside its current trading zone (515.65–524.43), with no trend and a tech market reported in a downtrend. A pullback to 504.96–512.76 would give a defined setup: stop below 486.0, first target 539.42.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-15 options price a 9.2% move, and that expiry closes before the 2027-01-27 report. So no new long-term money before that report's free cash flow figure, unless the price reaches 486.0–491.22.

change_mind: A close below 486.0, the bottom of the 8-touch support zone, would break the floor of the range and turn this to wait.
If the 2027-01-27 report shows trailing free cash flow climbing back from 60.0B toward 78.0B, the spending is paying back and holding becomes add.
If the next-year EPS estimate falls from 24.2 toward the 22.9 low, the earnings-based case weakens and the 220.42 cash-flow value matters more.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still a hold; the 1.12% drop to 517.99 came with no news and kept the price inside the 475.73–535.43 fair range.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
